title: 2-D Shapes: Polygons, Circles and Angles
seo_title: Grade 4 2-D Shapes and Angles Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, visualise and name 2-D shapes in the environment and geometric settings: regular and irregular polygons (triangles, squares, rectangles, other quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, heptagons) and circles; describe, sort and compare 2-D shapes in terms of straight and curved sides and number of sides; recognise and describe right angles, and angles bigger or smaller than right angles.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 2-D shapes worksheets: polygons and circles, regular and irregular polygons, right angles and comparing angles. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Count the straight sides to name a polygon.
key_sub: Compare angles with a right angle.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A polygon is a closed 2-D shape with straight sides: triangle (3), quadrilateral (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), heptagon (7), octagon (8).
  • A circle has one curved side and no corners.
  • A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles.
  • Compare angles with a right angle (the corner of a page): smaller than a right angle, a right angle, or bigger than a right angle.

Examples

Example

A shape with 6 straight sides

count the sides: 6

Answer: hexagon

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A turned shapeTurning does not change the name.
Equal sides onlyRegular needs equal angles too.
Long arms, big angleThe size of an angle is the turn, not the arm length.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about 2-D shapes?
faq.a: Recognise, visualise and name regular and irregular polygons (triangles, squares, rectangles, other quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, heptagons) and circles; describe, sort and compare them by straight and curved sides and number of sides; recognise right angles and angles smaller and greater than a right angle.
No. It has a curved side.

faq.q: How can learners check a right angle?
faq.a: Use the corner of a page.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and it has 6 straight sides that meet only at the corners, so it is a polygon.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: It is a square that has been turned. It is closed and has 4 straight sides, so it is a polygon. Turning a shape does not change that.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and has 3 straight sides. Every triangle is a polygon.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: It has 6 straight sides and it is closed. A polygon can have a corner that points in.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: The outline is 10 straight sides joined end to end. The sides do not cross, so the star is a polygon.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and every side is straight. The sides meet only at the corners, so it is a polygon.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and has 5 straight sides. The sides do not need to be the same length.
A circle is one curved line. It has no straight sides, so it is not a polygon.
An oval is curved all the way around. A polygon has only straight sides.
The bottom is straight, but the top is curved. A polygon has only straight sides.
The corners are curved. Even one curve means it is not a polygon.
Three sides are straight, but the left side is curved. Every side of a polygon must be straight.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: There is a gap at the bottom, so the shape is not closed. A polygon must be closed.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: The ends do not meet, so the shape is open. A polygon must be closed.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: Two sides cross in the middle. In a polygon the sides meet only at the corners.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: The lines cross each other inside the shape. In a polygon the sides meet only at the corners and never cross.
A is closed and has 6 straight sides. The others have a curve, are open, or have sides that cross.
B is made of two curved lines, so it is not a polygon. The other three are closed and have only straight sides.

items.q: A polygon is a closed shape made of …
items.e: A polygon is closed and all its sides are straight line segments. It can have 3 or more sides.

items.q: What is the smallest number of sides a polygon can have?
items.e: Two straight lines cannot close a shape. With 3 sides you get a triangle, the polygon with the fewest sides.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: It has 3 sides, so it is a triangle.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: It has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral. Its sides are all different, but it still has 4.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: It has 5 sides, so it is a pentagon.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: Count the sides around the outside: 2 roof sides, 2 walls and the bottom. That is 5 sides, so it is a pentagon.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: It has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: Go around the outside and count: 6 sides. It is a hexagon, even though it does not look like a honeycomb cell.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: It has 7 sides, so it is a heptagon.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: Count every side, including the short ones beside the point: 7 sides. It is a heptagon.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: It has 8 sides, so it is an octagon. Octo means 8, like an octopus with 8 arms.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: Kagiso the corner where you start, then count each side once: 8 sides. It is an octagon.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: It has 10 sides, so it is a decagon. Deca means 10.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: The star has 5 points, but count the sides: 2 sides for each point, 5 × 2 = 10. It is a decagon.

items.q: A polygon has 8 sides. What is it called?
items.e: 8 sides make an octagon. A stop sign is an octagon.

items.q: How many sides does a heptagon have?
items.e: A heptagon has 7 sides. Hexagon is 6, heptagon is 7, octagon is 8.

items.q: How many sides does a decagon have?
items.e: Deca means 10, so a decagon has 10 sides.

items.q: How many vertices does a hexagon have?
items.e: A polygon has the same number of vertices (corners) as sides. A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 vertices.

items.q: Ofentse counts the vertices of a polygon. There are 5. How many sides does it have?
items.e: Each side goes from one vertex to the next, so a polygon has as many sides as vertices: 5.

items.q: Which polygon has the most sides?
items.e: decagon 10, octagon 8, heptagon 7, hexagon 6. The decagon has the most.

items.q: Johan says, “A pentagon has 6 sides.” What is the mistake?
items.e: Penta means 5. A pentagon has 5 sides. A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon.

items.q: Which shape is a heptagon?
items.e: A has 7 sides. The others have 6, 8 and 5 sides.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 4 sides are equal and all 4 angles are right angles, so the square is a regular quadrilateral.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 3 sides are equal and all 3 angles are equal, so it is a regular triangle.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 5 sides are equal and all 5 angles are equal, so it is a regular pentagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 6 sides are equal and all 6 angles are equal, so it is a regular hexagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 8 sides are equal and all 8 angles are equal, so it is a regular octagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The 4 sides are equal, but 2 angles are narrow and 2 are wide. Equal sides alone do not make a polygon regular. This rhombus is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 6 sides are equal, but the angles are not all the same size, so the hexagon is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 4 angles are right angles, but the long sides and the short sides are different. The rectangle is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 6 angles are equal, but 3 sides are long and 3 are short, so the hexagon is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 8 angles are equal, but 4 sides are long and 4 are short, so the octagon is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The 3 sides are different lengths and only one angle is a right angle, so the triangle is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: Two sides are short and two are long, and the angles are different sizes, so it is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The sides are different lengths, and 2 angles are right angles while the others are wider. It is an irregular pentagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The top and bottom are different lengths, and the angles at the top are wider than at the bottom. The trapezium is irregular.

items.q: A regular polygon has …
c: all sides equal and all angles equal
items.e: A polygon is regular only when all its sides are equal AND all its angles are equal.

items.q: A rhombus that is not a square has 4 equal sides. Is it regular?
c: No, its angles are not all equal
Yes, its sides are all equal
items.e: Its sides are equal, but 2 angles are wide and 2 are narrow. A regular polygon needs equal angles too.

items.q: A rectangle that is not a square has 4 right angles. Is it regular?
c: No, it has no right angles
Yes, all its angles are equal
No, its sides are not all equal
items.e: Its angles are equal, but the long sides and short sides are different. A regular polygon needs equal sides too.

items.q: What do we call a regular quadrilateral?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 equal angles (right angles). It is the only regular quadrilateral.

items.q: Which polygon is regular?
items.e: C has 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles. The rhombus has unequal angles, the rectangle has unequal sides, and the kite has neither.

items.q: Which polygon is irregular?
items.e: B is a rhombus. Its sides are equal, but its angles are not. The other three are regular.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (a square corner), so it is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (a square corner), so it is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (a square corner), so it is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (a square corner), so it is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle (90°).

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle (90°). Turning an angle does not change its size.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle (90°). Turning an angle does not change its size.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line, so it is obtuse.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line, so it is obtuse.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line, so it is obtuse.
The two arms point in opposite directions and make a straight line. That is two right angles (180°).

items.q: Which angle is acute?
items.e: Picture A is smaller than a right angle. The others are a right angle, an obtuse angle and a straight line.

items.q: Which angle is obtuse?
items.e: Picture B is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line. A straight line is two right angles, not an obtuse angle.

items.q: Which angle is a right angle?
items.e: Picture C has the small square that shows a right angle. It is turned, but turning does not change an angle.

items.q: Ofentse says this angle is acute because its arms are short. Is she right?
c: Yes, short arms make it acute
No, it is a right angle
Yes, it is a small angle
items.e: The size of an angle is how far it opens, not how long its arms are. This angle opens wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse.

items.q: Lindiwe says this is not a right angle because it is turned. Is she right?
c: No, it is a straight line
No, it is still a right angle
items.e: The small square shows a square corner. Turning an angle does not change its size, so it is still a right angle.

items.q: What is an acute angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle (less than 90°).

items.q: What is an obtuse angle?
c: between a right angle and a straight line
items.e: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°).

items.q: How many right angles make a straight line?
items.e: A right angle is 90° and a straight line is 180°. 90° + 90° = 180°, so 2 right angles make a straight line.

items.q: A right angle is a quarter turn. How many degrees is a right angle?
items.e: A right angle is 90°. A straight line (two right angles) is 180°.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Angle Q is obtuse and angle P is acute. Q is larger, even though its arms are shorter.
Angle P is obtuse and angle Q is acute. Long arms do not make an angle larger.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both angles open the same amount. Only the arms are different lengths, and arm length does not change an angle.
Angle Q is reflex: its arc goes round the outside, past a straight angle. Angle P is obtuse, less than a straight angle.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both are right angles (the small squares show it). Tilting an angle or making its arms longer does not change it.
Angle P is reflex, so it is greater than a straight angle. Angle Q is obtuse, less than a straight angle.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both are acute, but angle Q opens wider. Put one on top of the other to check.
Angle P is a straight angle. Angle Q is obtuse: it is less than a straight angle, even with longer arms.

items.q: Which angle is the largest?
items.e: B is obtuse, so it is greater than a right angle. A and D are acute and C is a right angle. B has the shortest arms, but arm length does not matter.
C is acute: less than a right angle. A is obtuse, B is a right angle and D is reflex.
Only the arc in D goes round more than a straight angle. A is obtuse: close to a straight angle, but less.
A is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle. In B the gap looks obtuse, but the arc marks the reflex angle round the outside.
Y is acute, X is obtuse and Z is reflex. Look at the turn and the arc, not the arm length.

items.q: Which is always larger: an obtuse angle or an acute angle?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle. An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle. So the obtuse angle is always larger.

items.q: Which is always larger: a straight angle or a reflex angle?
items.e: A reflex angle is greater than a straight angle, by definition.

items.q: Angle P is a right angle. Angle Q is a little less than a right angle. Which angle is larger?
items.e: Angle Q is less than a right angle, so the right angle P is larger.

items.q: Anika draws two angles. Angle P has arms 10 cm long and angle Q has arms 3 cm long. She says P must be the larger angle. Is she right?
c: Yes, longer arms make a larger angle
No, arm length does not change the size of an angle
items.e: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between the arms. You cannot tell which is larger from the arm lengths.

items.q: Which of these angles is smaller than a right angle?
items.e: Only an acute angle is less than a right angle. Obtuse, straight and reflex angles are all larger.

items.q: Two angles are both obtuse. What do you know for sure?
c: Both are larger than a straight angle
Both are larger than a right angle
items.e: Every obtuse angle is greater than a right angle and less than a straight angle. Two obtuse angles can still be different sizes.

items.q: An angle is larger than 2 right angles but smaller than 4 right angles. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: 2 right angles make a straight angle and 4 make a revolution. Between them is a reflex angle.
